Verified and correct as written: Lullaby Trust head sinks no more than a few millimetres, sleep bags usually from about 4 kg, blankets no higher than shoulders, pillows, quilts and duvets raise SIDS risk 3 times, weighted swaddles, blankets and sleeping bags on the Lullaby Trust avoid list, pods and nests, hammocks, positioners, bouncers and swings, and standards not meaning a product reduces SIDS risk. AAP 10 degree incline and no weighted products. CPSC 10 degrees and weighted products. NHS sling fabric not covering head. Which? 89% satisfied with second-hand pushchair (2024 survey), EN 1888, EN 1930, lead paint before 1973, loose stickers, monitor passwords, drawstrings, hooded novelty sleeping bags, button batteries and magnets. RSA: R44 seats no longer sold in the EU from 1 September 2024 and seats in use remain legal. BFU 4.5 to 6.5 cm bar gaps and EN 716 (August 2016). Michigan MDHHS: use only the mattress sold with a pack and play. NIJZ 2020 advises against folding cots with taut mesh sides because of injury risk. Aldi figures 30%, 62%, 30% shoes at £33, over a quarter for mittens and dressing gowns, 78% emotional support, research by Mortar January 2024, press release 2 February 2024. ParentData about 1,400 respondents in 2024, carrier most popular best item, feeding pillow at the midpoint, bouncers, monitors and gyms on both lists, sleep sacks high, nappy cream spatula a surprise. Mumsnet Tesco advertisement feature with affiliate links, about 41 essentials plus 7 nice-to-haves, updated 18 July 2025, no do not buy list. Mumsnet 2020 thread: nappy bin 'complete waste of money', white noise app 'best money I ever spent'.

Bar spacing differs by source: BFU gives 4.5 to 6.5 cm (matching EN 716), NIJZ gives 4.5 to 6.0 cm and Which? gives 2.5 to 6.5 cm. The article follows BFU and EN 716, which is defensible. The editor may want to mention NIJZ for Slovenian readers.
The R44 sale ban sentence is limited to the EU, which is correct. Rules for retailers in Great Britain may differ, so UK readers should not read it as a UK rule.
The RSA page could not be fetched directly (Cloudflare block). Its content was confirmed through a fetch tool, but the link title 'ISOFIX and i-Size' could not be confirmed against the page heading.
The Mumsnet 2018 thread has 6 pages and only page 1 could be checked.

Headline and meta: '8 things' and 'Parents say you need 8 first' are an editorial count built from the Mumsnet thread's short core list, not a number parents gave. Acceptable as a hook, but the meta description 'Top lists run to 48 items' refers to 1 list (Mumsnet and Tesco). Consider 'The best-known list runs to 48 items'.
Mesh travel cots: the article fairly states that US and Slovenian advice differ. Hoppo's own suggestion is labelled as Hoppo's.
